bug_semantics: An attacker who can post to a Telegram group can store HTML in a message's content. The search/list UI passed that database-backed item.content to highlightKeyword(), which returned the text unchanged when no keyword was present and otherwise performed only a regex replacement that inserted a highlight span; neither branch escaped the message text. Vue then interpreted the returned string through v-html, so merely viewing/searching the shared messages rendered attacker markup and could execute an event-handler payload such as in another user's browser.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructable BIC is PR #145 member 6454fcaf810d2cd92d9010dffc6b14b3acfa0ad7 (feat: global search). It created apps/frontend/src/components/GlobalSearch.vue with both the unescaped highlightKeyword implementation and the v-html sink over item.content. GitHub squash 4fec95f79a6215d61e92f572baefef9379632d55 later landed the PR on the main lineage; subsequent renames, copies, and consolidations preserved the mechanism until it reached apps/web/src/components/messages/MessageList.vue, so those later commits are not introducers.

Within that member history, git log -S'highlightKeyword' isolates 6454fcaf810d2cd92d9010dffc6b14b3acfa0ad7; its diff creates apps/frontend/src/components/GlobalSearch.vue and writes highlightKeyword plus v-html="highlightKeyword(item.content, keyword)" together. Any Cursor/Bugbot disclosure appears on this later fix PR, not on the BIC commit object, and therefore does not attribute the introduction.
reasoning: The vulnerable dataflow is attacker-controlled Telegram message content -> stored CoreMessage.content -> highlightKeyword without HTML neutralization -> Vue v-html -> browser execution in another group participant's search/list view. Although the advisory names MessageList.vue, history proves that component was a later consolidation: the unsafe function and sink originated in GlobalSearch.vue. The main-line squash 4fec95f79a6215d61e92f572baefef9379632d55 is an aggregate, so its publicly retained PR #145 head was decomposed. Member 6454fcaf810d2cd92d9010dffc6b14b3acfa0ad7 is the smallest commit that writes both causal halves, and its immediate parent lacks both the file and any frontend highlightKeyword/v-html mechanism. The squash landing precedes and is contained in vulnerable v1.2.8; the advisory fix is absent from that tag, then contained in the safe v1.3.1 tag. The direct remediation is 40155a70764e85ddf995ea3ce11a7671b9a6ef9b and the final landed fix is 54f6adced844ce9990228d75e31348bfed934e05. Because the only permissible attribution source—the raw BIC commit object—shows a human author/committer and no AI marker, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
